title: Male Reproductive System: Testes, Vasa Efferentia, & Bidder's Canal
topic: Mesorchium, 10–12 Vasa Efferentia, Bidder's Canal, & Urinogenital Duct
quickSummary: The male reproductive system consists of paired yellowish ovoid testes suspended from the kidneys by the Mesorchium. Sperm exit via 10–12 Vasa Efferentia into Bidder's Canal inside the kidney, pass through kidney collecting tubules into the Urinogenital Duct (ureter), and discharge through the Cloaca. Sperm thus traverses the kidney parenchyma in males.

conceptBreakdown.content:
The male reproductive apparatus is anatomically and physiologically intertwined with the mesonephric kidneys.

### Primary Structures
• **Testes**: Paired compact, yellowish, ovoid organs attached to the anterodorsal border of each kidney by a double peritoneal fold called the **Mesorchium**.
• **Vasa Efferentia**: **10 to 12 fine ductules** arising from the testes that traverse the mesorchium, penetrate the kidney, and open into Bidder’s Canal.
• **Bidder's Canal**: A specialized longitudinal canal located along the medial margin of the mesonephric kidney that receives spermatozoa.
• **Urinogenital Duct**: Sperm passes from Bidder's canal into transverse kidney collecting tubules, exiting via the **Urinogenital Duct (male ureter)** into the **Cloaca**.
